metadata.description: Phase-transition database for elemental systems.  For each element the ordered phase sequence (solid polymorphs → liquid → gas) is listed with cumulative enthalpies and entropies relative to the DFT ground state (H = 0, S = 0).  Only solid polymorphs possessing BOTH a DFT energy (from Materials Project) AND a known transition temperature (from literature) are retained.  Liquid and gas phases are always included.
metadata.policy: Tiered unary data policy (2026-08-04): Tier A removes spurious MP structures (no ambient-pressure stability field at any T; see gliquid_python/src/gliquid/reference/spurious_structures.json) before ground-state selection; Tier B emits a per-element 'lattice_stabilities' block (BCC/FCC/HCP cumulative enthalpies above the anchor, no transition temperature required; MP primary, omegas-file fallback); Tier C re-anchors elements where GGA misranks two real phases (Co, Sm) and substitutes SGTE lattice stabilities for the displaced phases, with machine-readable provenance. Metastable-entropy exception (2026-08-07): six HCP lattice stabilities (Au, Li, Ba, Ca, Cu, Ag) carry an imported SGTE entropy instead of the convention's 0.0 -- see the 'metastable_entropy_exception' convention below. Virtual-polymorph injection (2026-08-07): four real equilibrium phases absent from Materials Project entirely (beta-Y bcc, beta-Sc bcc, gamma-Sm bcc, gamma-Mn fcc) are injected onto their ladders, closing the Tier A/B/C gap for a structure that is real but has no MP record -- see the 'virtual_polymorphs' convention below.

conventions.reference_state: The DFT ground state (lowest T = 0 K energy per atom from Materials Project after the Tier A blacklist and Tier C re-anchoring) defines H = 0, S = 0 for each element. After the 2026-08-04 audit the anchor matches the experimentally stable structure; audited real low-T allotropes (Na hP4, Li 9R, alpha-Sn, omega-Ti) keep the low-T structure as anchor.
conventions.lattice_stabilities: Per-element block of cumulative BCC/FCC/HCP enthalpies above the anchor for structures NOT on the phase ladder, with no transition temperature -- solid-solution end-member references only; they never enter the ladder, the liquid stacking, or the hull line compounds. delta_S = 0 by the recalculation convention (no transition temperature to divide by), EXCEPT for the six entries listed under 'metastable_entropy_exception'. Sources: MP polymorph energies (primary), omegas_hcp.json (fallback, anchored per gliquid.solution._apply_omegas_fallback's math).
conventions.metastable_entropy_exception: Scoped, explicitly-keyed departure from the recalculation convention, authorised 2026-08-07 on the evidence of dev/data/ss_reference_state_audit.md (defect_class == 'metastable_flat'). A metastable structure has no stability field, hence no transition temperature, hence delta_S = 0 by construction -- so its free energy stays pinned at its 0 K enthalpy while SGTE says it should climb (~2.1 kJ/mol at Tm for hcp-Au, which leaves spurious HCP solid-solution fields on fitted diagrams). For six HCP lattice stabilities -- Au -1.6, Li -0.7, Ba -1.3, Ca -0.7, Cu -0.2, Ag -0.3 J/(mol K) -- the ENTHALPY is unchanged (still DFT/omegas) and only the ENTROPY is imported, as SGTE's -b from the dG = a + b*T lattice stability, taken as a difference against the DFT anchor phase rather than an absolute SER offset. Every value is NEGATIVE, which is what makes the change safe: the endpoint melting reconstruction takes max((h_liq - dH_i) / (s_liq - dS_i)), and a negative delta_S only enlarges the denominator, so the reference can move further below the ground state but never overtake it. Rh HCP is deliberately EXCLUDED (GHCPRH = 3000 - 0.5*T gives delta_S = +0.5, positive) and keeps delta_S = 0. Per-entry provenance rides in each entry's metadata as 'entropy_source' / 'entropy_basis'; the scope is the table build_phase_transitions.METASTABLE_ENTROPY_OVERRIDES, enforced by a build-time invariant. Ladder phases are NOT affected: every thermodynamically stable phase keeps deriving its entropy as delta_H / T_trans.
conventions.virtual_polymorphs: A phase that is a genuine 1 atm equilibrium allotrope but has NO Materials Project entry of that spacegroup falls through Tier A (blacklist), Tier B (lattice stability) and Tier C (re-anchor) alike, and a POLYMORPH_TRANSITION_T key would have nothing to attach to. Such a phase is injected onto the ladder from build_phase_transitions.VIRTUAL_POLYMORPHS, carrying a cited transition temperature and an ANCHORED SGTE enthalpy -- a difference against a phase shared by both frames (SGTE's zero is GHSER<EL>, this database's is the MP ground-state total energy), never a raw SER offset. NO ENTROPY IS IMPORTED: the injected phase is thermodynamically stable, so it keeps the delta_S = delta_H / T_trans convention like every other ladder phase. Injected 2026-08-07 on the evidence of dev/data/ss_reference_state_audit.md (defect_class == 'missing_real_transition'): beta-Y (bcc, 1751 K, 4886.73 J/mol), beta-Sc (bcc, 1610 K, 4016.50), gamma-Sm (bcc, 1345 K, 2687) and gamma-Mn (fcc, 1368 K, 3602.96), alongside the pre-existing re-entrant delta-Fe (1667 K, 1737). Consequences: a real ladder phase SUPERSEDES the metastable lattice stability of the same spacegroup, so Y and Sc lose their BCC 'lattice_stabilities' entries (+11987.46 / +10161.50 J/mol, 2.5x the assessed transition enthalpy); Y, Sc and Sm gain a solid step, so their liquid H and S rise; gamma-Mn instead SPLITS the existing beta->delta step, because delta-Mn's 6308 J/mol is already cumulative alpha->beta->gamma->delta, so Mn's liquid enthalpy is unchanged and only its entropy stack re-splits. A build-time invariant requires every injected phase to survive the LIS filter and to be strictly bracketed in BOTH enthalpy and transition temperature by its ladder neighbours.
conventions.known_ground_state_conflicts: build_phase_transitions.KNOWN_GS_CONFLICTS declares (element, structure) pairs whose omegas-file DFT energy the 2026-08-04 audit found untrustworthy -- Mn HCP, where GGA magnetism ranks hcp ~3.1 kJ/mol BELOW alpha-Mn. No omegas-derived lattice stability is emitted for a declared pair, and the declaration is checked BEFORE the sign, because it is a statement about the source energy rather than about how one particular anchoring landed: the fallback anchors on the lowest-omegas-energy shared phase, so putting a new phase on the ladder can flip the anchor and turn a refused negative into a plausible-looking positive built from the same rejected energy (gamma-Mn on the ladder moves Mn's anchor from BCC to FCC and would otherwise have emitted hcp-Mn at +779 J/mol, against SGTE's assessed +3870.5). An UNDECLARED negative is still a hard build error. A declared pair that never fires is also a hard error, so a stale declaration cannot mask a later regression -- Mn FCC was retired on 2026-08-07 when gamma-Mn filled that slot from the ladder.
conventions.cumulative_enthalpy: H(phase) = DFT enthalpy above GS for solid polymorphs; H(liquid) = H(last solid) + H_fusion; H(gas) = H(liquid) + H_vaporization.
conventions.cumulative_entropy: S is accumulated stepwise: at each transition i, ΔS_i = ΔH_i / T_i, where ΔH_i = H_i − H_{i−1} and T_i is the transition temperature.  S(phase) = Σ ΔS_j for all j ≤ i.
conventions.enthalpy_ordering_filter: Among all solid polymorphs with known transition temperatures, the largest subset maintaining strictly increasing enthalpy with increasing temperature is retained.  A longest-increasing-subsequence (LIS) algorithm selects the maximum number of phases; ties are broken by preferring earlier (lower-T) phases.
conventions.no_heat_capacity: No Cp integration is performed. Enthalpy is treated as a step function that changes only at phase transition temperatures.
conventions.null_values: null indicates data not available from the queried sources.
